name: The SDET Architect
techName: src/agents/sdet-architect/ — inventory.ts · parsers/{common,cfamily,selenium-*,cucumber,postman}.ts · locators.ts · generators/{plan,steps,pages,spec,bdd,api,project}.ts · convert.ts · report.ts · index.ts
oneLiner: Inventories any legacy test estate (Selenium in any language, Cucumber, Postman, test plans) and rebuilds it as one standardised Playwright + Playwright MCP architecture, offline.
lead: Point it at a folder. It classifies every file, parses Java, Python, C# and JavaScript Selenium (plus Cypress, Cucumber features and step definitions, Postman collections and markdown test plans) into one intermediate model with regex and line-based parsers — no AST libraries, no language runtimes — standardises every locator into the most robust Playwright form with a confidence score, and generates a single project: page objects, fixtures, specs, playwright-bdd steps, API specs, config, CI, `.mcp.json` and a `MIGRATION.md` that lists every line it could not convert with its source `file:line`. On the bundled fabricated estate (run `46f19623`, 2026-09-11) it scanned 12 files, found 28 tests, converted 24 fully and 2 partially, left 2 as `test.fixme` scaffolds, emitted 99 of 108 steps as Playwright (**91.7%**), standardised 38 unique locators with 3 below the 0.60 review line, and wrote 26 files. With `LLM_PROVIDER=none` the output is byte-for-byte deterministic.
chore: Every engagement starts with archaeology. A `selenium-java` module nobody has run since the last Chrome upgrade, a Python folder a contractor left behind, a .NET project that builds on one laptop, a `.feature` file whose step definitions drifted, a Postman collection with the real API expectations buried in `pm.test` scripts, and a markdown test plan that is the only honest description of what the business cares about. Someone senior spends three weeks reading all of it, keeps a spreadsheet of locators, hand-writes Playwright — and the spreadsheet is stale the day it is finished.
instead: One run. One architecture. A `MIGRATION.md` with a per-file status table, a numbered TODO list where every row carries its source `file:line`, a locator-confidence histogram, and findings in five categories. The human work is the TODO list, not the reading.
whyItMatters: The [process page](../process.html) puts this agent underneath the eval cube as the deterministic regression layer: an organisation cannot tell whether an AI deployment broke something unless its existing tests run, and they usually do not. Standardising them onto Playwright + MCP is also what lets an MCP client reuse the same page objects the specs use for exploratory checks.

howItWorks.step: Walks the estate, skipping build output and virtual environments by default, reads every text file under 2 MB, and classifies it from its extension plus its content: `.feature`, known config names, Java / Python / C# / JS by annotations and imports, JSON only if it carries a Postman schema, markdown only if it looks like a test plan.
howItWorks.explain: Classification is a pure function on `(path, content)` so it is unit-tested without a filesystem. A `.java` file with `@Given/@When/@Then` is `step-definitions`; with `@Test` it is `selenium-java`; with only `org.openqa.selenium` imports it is `page-object`. The same three-way split exists for Python (`@given`, `def test_*`, `find_element`) and C# (`[Given]`, `[Test]`, `OpenQA.Selenium`). Binary files are detected by a NUL byte in the first 512 bytes; a `.docx` or `.xlsx` whose name says "test plan" is still inventoried as one. The fixture estate came out as `selenium-java` 2, `selenium-python` 1, `selenium-csharp` 1, `selenium-js` 1, `cucumber-feature` 1, `step-definitions` 1, `page-object` 1, `postman-collection` 1, `test-plan` 1, `config` 2.

howItWorks.step: Parses brace languages structurally without an AST: strips comments while preserving line numbers, finds classes with a string-aware brace matcher, collects `@FindBy` / `By` fields, string constants and page-object fields, then splits each method body into `;`-terminated statements.
howItWorks.explain: `stripCComments` replaces block comments with the same number of newlines, so every `Step.line` still points at the real source line — that is what makes the `[file:line]` on each TODO trustworthy. A method's annotations decide what it is: a test annotation (`@Test`, `[Fact]`, `[TestMethod]` …) makes a `TestCase`, a hook annotation (`@BeforeMethod`, `[SetUp]`, `@BeforeAll` …) a `Hook`, a step annotation a `StepDefinition` with its Cucumber expression compiled to a regex, and in a page-object file every other public method becomes a `PageMethod`. Class-level fields seed the lexical `Scope` every method body is parsed with, which is how `usernameInput.sendKeys(user)` inside `LoginPage.login` knows that `usernameInput` is `By.id("username")`.

howItWorks.step: Normalises one statement into a token string: string literals become `«S0»`, `By(...)` locators `«L0»`, `findElement(...)` wrappers `«E0»`, variables known from scope are substituted, and browser reads (`getText`, `getTitle`, `isDisplayed`, `size()`) become typed values `«V0»`.
howItWorks.explain: The same engine serves Java, C#, JavaScript and Python because it never looks at syntax, only at the shapes Selenium code takes: `By.id("x")`, `(By.ID, "x")`, `find_element_by_id("x")`, `$("css")`, `cy.get("css")` all become the same `«L»` token. Tokenising strings first means a locator value containing a semicolon or a parenthesis cannot confuse later regexes. Variable substitution uses a word-boundary regex over the tokenised text, so `cartBadge.getText()` becomes `«V0»` with `{ type: 'text', locator: By.id("cart-count") }` and the assertion two lines later can be typed. `resolveConcat` folds `BASE_URL + "/catalog"` using class constants, which is why the generated spec says `page.goto('/catalog')` after the base URL is stripped.

howItWorks.step: Classifies the normalised statement into a `Step`: an assignment updates the scope and emits nothing; driver lifecycle noise is dropped; then navigate, click / fill / select / press / hover, hard or explicit wait, assertion, typed return, page-object call — or `unknown`.
howItWorks.explain: Order matters. `WebElement cartBadge = driver.findElement(By.id("cart-count"))` is an assignment: it binds `cartBadge` in scope and produces no step. `driver.manage().window().maximize()` matches `NOISE_RE` and is dropped. `Thread.sleep(2000)` is a **hard** wait (2000 ms; Python `time.sleep(3)` is scaled to 3000) and will be emitted as a NOTE plus a flakiness finding. `new WebDriverWait(...).until(visibilityOfElementLocated(By.id("checkout-button")))` is an explicit wait on a locator and becomes `waitFor({ state: 'visible' })`. `parseAssertion` understands TestNG/JUnit `assertEquals(actual, expected)`, NUnit `Assert.That(x, Is.EqualTo(y))`, pytest `assert a == b` / `in`, chai `expect(x).to.equal(y)`, Node `assert.strictEqual`, and Cypress `.should('have.text', y)`, and maps the typed value to a Playwright assertion (`text` → `toHaveText`, `title` → `toHaveTitle`, `count` → `toHaveCount`, `visible` → `toBeVisible`). Anything else is `unknown` and becomes a TODO.

howItWorks.step: Standardises every locator into the most robust Playwright form with a 0–1 confidence: ids 0.95 (0.5 when they look generated), `name` 0.85, `linkText` → `getByRole('link')` 0.9, simple xpaths reduced to css / `getByText` / `getByRole`, absolute xpaths kept as `xpath=` at 0.20. Anything under 0.60 becomes a `locator` finding.
howItWorks.explain: The xpath reducer walks segment by segment: `//div[@class='product-card'][1]//button[contains(text(),'Add to cart')]` becomes `div[class="product-card"]:nth-of-type(1) button:has-text("Add to cart")` at 0.50 with the note "positional index in xpath"; `//p[text()='Your cart is empty']` becomes `getByText('Your cart is empty', { exact: true })`; `//a[text()='Cart']` would become `getByRole('link', …)` because `ROLE_TAGS` knows `a` is a link. `/html/body/div[2]/…` is never reduced: it stays `xpath=` at 0.20 and lands in the report's low-confidence table. `chooseTestIdAttribute` looks at the whole estate first, so if the legacy code used `[data-qa=…]` everywhere, the generated `playwright.config.ts` sets `testIdAttribute: 'data-qa'` and those become `getByTestId`. Fixture result: 15 locators at 0.90+, 17 at 0.80–0.89, 3 at 0.60–0.79, 2 at 0.40–0.59, 1 below 0.40.

howItWorks.step: Plans the architecture: one page class per detected page object plus one synthetic page per test class that used locators inline, unique class and file names, camelCase field names derived from each locator, and one fixture per page so specs can destructure them.
howItWorks.explain: `LoginPage.java` is a real page object, so it becomes `src/pages/Login.page.ts` with its five fields and four methods. `CheckoutTest.java` used `By.id("search-box")` and friends inline, so it gets a **synthetic** `CheckoutPage` whose fields are exactly those locators, deduplicated by `strategy:value`, named by `fieldNameFor` (`search-box` → `searchBox`, `linkText Cart` → `cartLink`, `.cart-line` → `cartLine`, `//p[text()='Your cart is empty']` → `yourCartIsEmptyText`). The fixture file then exports `test` extended with `loginPage`, `checkoutPage`, `searchPage`, … so the generated spec reads `async ({ page, checkoutPage, loginPage })`. Fixture parameter lists are filled in **after** the bodies are emitted, because only then is it known which pages a test touched.

howItWorks.step: Emits each `Step` as one line of Playwright, or as `// TODO(sdet-architect): <original>  [file:line]` when a value, target or page object cannot be resolved; hard waits become a `NOTE` comment plus a flakiness finding; a test that is half TODOs is generated with `test.fixme`.
howItWorks.explain: Everything the emitter needs is in the `Step`: for `fill`, a literal value or a method parameter name (anything else is a TODO "value is not a literal or parameter"); for `select`, whether the source selected by visible text, by value or by index; for `assert`, the typed target and whether it was negated. `navigate` strips the detected base URL so specs use `baseURL` from config. A `call` step resolves the page-object class to its fixture name, so `loginPage.login(QA_USER, QA_PASS)` in Java becomes `await loginPage.login('qa.buyer@example.test', 'Secret123!')` with the constants inlined. `statusOf` is what the MIGRATION.md status column means: 0 TODOs converted, under half partial, half or more manual with `test.fixme`. On the fixture, `legacyHelperOnly` has 1 TODO in 3 steps → partial; both markdown test plans are 100% TODO → manual.

howItWorks.step: Assembles the whole estate in memory — page classes, fixtures, UI specs, `.feature` files kept verbatim with playwright-bdd step definitions, Postman requests as `request`-fixture specs, config, CI — records findings in five categories, and writes `MIGRATION.md` last.
howItWorks.explain: `generateEstate` is pure: files in a `Map<string,string>`, statuses, TODOs, flaky waits, tests without assertions, duplicated locators, low-confidence locators and totals out. `index.ts` is the only place that touches disk, the database and the optional model: it writes the map (unless `dry_run`), adds one `artifacts` row per file with a kind (`page-object`, `playwright-spec`, `migration-report`, `project-file`), and adds findings — `locator` (high below 0.40, else medium), `conversion` (medium), `flakiness`, `duplication` and `quality` (low). Because the report is built from the same objects, the counts in `MIGRATION.md` and in `GET /runs/:id/findings` cannot disagree. Fixture run: conversion 9, flakiness 4, duplication 9, quality 3, locator 3. The `preview` route runs the same pipeline on one file with no disk and no database.

LoginPage.java (PageFactory) → src/pages/Login.page.ts (status: converted, 4/4 methods)

examples.output: Output JSON: files_scanned 12, tests_found 28, tests_converted 24, tests_partial 2, tests_manual 2, locators_total 38, locators_low_confidence 3, coverage_pct 91.7. `MIGRATION.md`: per-file table with 10 rows (LoginPage.java converted 4/4; AccountTests.cs, profile.test.js, test_cart.py, SearchTest.java converted 3/3 each; CheckoutTest.java partial 2+1; login.feature converted 3 scenarios with its LoginSteps.java "kept"; shop-api collection partial 3+1; regression-test-plan.md manual 0/2). TODO list of 9: seven are the two markdown test-plan cases (every step is a TODO by definition), one is `takeScreenshotAndUpload(driver, "account")`, one is the Postman body assertion `pm.expect(body.sku).to.eql('sku-1001')`. Locator confidence 15 / 17 / 3 / 2 / 1 across the five buckets; by source strategy id 11, css 9, xpath 7, linkText 4, name 3, className 2, partialLinkText 1, tagName 1. Three low-confidence rows: the positional xpath (0.50), the absolute xpath (0.20) and a bare `h1` tag (0.50). Findings: conversion 9, flakiness 4, duplication 9, quality 3, locator 3. 26 files generated, including `tests/features/login.feature` verbatim, `tests/steps/login.steps.ts` with `Given/When/Then` from `createBdd`, and `tests/api/shop-api.spec.ts` with collection variables overridable by environment variable.

underHood.heading: Inventory
underHood.whenRuns: Phase a, the only part that reads the filesystem.
underHood.output: One `InventoryEntry` per file (path, kind, bytes, lines, language) and a `Map` of contents — via `inventory()`, `globToRegExp()`, `classifyFile()`.

underHood.heading: The intermediate model
underHood.whenRuns: Phase b, every parser targets it.
underHood.output: A `TestSuite`: `tests[]`, `pageObjects[]`, `hooks[]`, `locators[]`, `urls[]`, `constants`, plus `feature`, `stepDefinitions` or `requests` for the non-Selenium kinds; every `Step` carries `kind`, `locator`, `value` / `valueExpr`, `assertion`, `raw` and `line` — see `model.ts`.

underHood.heading: Normalisation and scope
underHood.whenRuns: Per statement, inside every method body.
underHood.input: One statement and the method's `Scope` (elements, By variables, typed values, page-object variables, parameters, constants).
underHood.output: A token string such as `«E0».sendKeys(«S1»)` and the side tables that resolve the tokens — via `normalize()`, `resolveConcat()`.

underHood.heading: Locator confidence
underHood.whenRuns: Once per unique `strategy:value`, cached in the plan.
underHood.output: A `StdLocator` with `expr`, `confidence` and a `note` when it is under 0.60 — via `standardize()`, `standardizeXpath()`, `chooseTestIdAttribute()`.

underHood.heading: Plan, pages, fixtures
underHood.whenRuns: Phase c, before any code is emitted.
underHood.output: Planned pages with unique class names, files, fixture names and fields; `src/fixtures/index.ts` extending `test` with one fixture per page — via `buildPlan()`, `genFixtures()`.

underHood.heading: Findings and MIGRATION.md
underHood.whenRuns: Phase d, after generation, before the write.
underHood.output: Rows in `findings` (locator, conversion, flakiness, duplication, quality) and the eight-section report — via `run()` and `buildMigrationReport()`.

underHood.heading: Preview, no disk, no database
underHood.output: `{ kind, output_file, spec, tests_found, todos, coverage_pct }` for that one file — via `preview()`, the same parsers and generators, nothing written.

prerequisites: Node 24 and `npm install` in the repo. No Java, Python or .NET toolchain is needed: the parsers read text.
A folder with the legacy estate, given as an **absolute** path. The bundled `fixtures/sdet-architect` is a fabricated one you can try first.
Optionally the real application's base URL; otherwise the most common navigated origin in the estate is detected.

steps.label: Install and initialise
steps.why: Same database as the Forward Deployed Tester; both agents write to `data/forward-qa.db`.

steps.label: Run it on the bundled fabricated estate
steps.why: Twelve files across Java (JUnit-style page object, TestNG tests, Cucumber steps), Python (pytest), C# (NUnit), JavaScript (selenium-webdriver + mocha), a `.feature`, a Postman collection, a markdown test plan and two config files. The CLI prints the output JSON and the path of `MIGRATION.md`.
steps.firstRun: Run `46f19623` on 2026-09-11: 12 files, 28 tests, 24 / 2 / 2, 38 locators, 3 low, 91.7% coverage, 26 files written.
steps.rerun: Byte-for-byte identical output under `LLM_PROVIDER=none`; a new run id and directory each time.

steps.label: Run it on a real estate
steps.cmd:
npm run agent:sdet -- --src /abs/path/to/legacy-tests --org acme --base-url https://app.acme.example.test
npm run agent:sdet -- --src /abs/path/to/legacy-tests --org acme --include "**/*.java" --exclude "**/archive/**"
npm run agent:sdet -- --src /abs/path/to/legacy-tests --org acme --dry-run
steps.why: `--include` / `--exclude` are globs relative to `source_dir` and add to the default excludes. `--dry-run` computes everything, records nothing to disk, and still returns the full `MIGRATION.md` text in the output JSON — useful for a first look at coverage before committing to a workspace.

steps.label: Read MIGRATION.md top-down
steps.why: Eight sections: header numbers, inventory, per-file status, the TODO list, locator confidence, findings summary, the generated tree, next steps, and how to run from an MCP client. Every TODO row carries the same `[file:line]` that appears as a comment in the generated code, so `grep -rn "TODO(sdet-architect)"` in the output gives the same list.

steps.label: Typecheck and run the generated project
steps.cmd:
cd workspace/<run_id>/playwright
npm install
npx playwright install --with-deps
npm run typecheck
BASE_URL=https://staging.acme.example.test npm test -- --project=chromium
steps.why: The end-to-end test in the repo (`tests/sdet-architect/e2e.test.ts`) already compiles the generated project with `tsc`, so `typecheck` is the first gate. For the fabricated estate the base URL `https://shop.example.test` does not exist, so `npm test` there fails at navigation by design; against a real estate, run one spec at a time and work the TODO list.
steps.firstRun: On the fixture estate `typecheck` passes; the specs cannot pass because the site is fictional.

steps.label: Convert one file without touching disk
steps.cmd:
npm start
curl -s -X POST localhost:8787/agents/sdet-architect/preview -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"language\":\"java\",\"code\":$(jq -Rs . < LoginTest.java)}" | jq -r .spec
steps.why: The preview route classifies, parses, plans and generates for a single file and returns the spec text plus `tests_found`, `todos` and `coverage_pct`. Nothing is written and no run row is created — a good way to show a sceptical team what their `LoginTest.java` becomes.

steps.label: Drive the generated pages from an MCP client
steps.cmd:
cd workspace/<run_id>/playwright
npm run mcp    # mcp-server-playwright --config playwright-mcp.config.json
steps.why: `.mcp.json` and `playwright-mcp.config.json` are generated with the project. An MCP client can navigate to the base URL and use `src/pages/*.page.ts` as the vocabulary for exploratory checks — the same locators the specs use.

steps.label: Run the agent's own tests
steps.why: Parsers for every dialect, the locator table, the emitters, the inventory and one end-to-end run over the fixture that also `tsc`-compiles the output.
steps.firstRun: Part of the 89 green tests on 2026-09-11.

inputs.name: --src / source_dir
inputs.desc: Absolute path to the legacy estate.

inputs.name: --org / org_slug
inputs.desc: Names the generated package (`<org>-playwright`) and the report.

inputs.name: --include, --exclude
inputs.desc: Globs relative to the estate; `**`, `*`, `?`, `{a,b}` supported.

inputs.name: --base-url / base_url
inputs.desc: Optional; else detected from the most common navigated origin, ignoring `api.*` hosts.

outputs.name: Rows in findings and artifacts
outputs.desc: Five finding categories; one artifact per generated file with its kind.

outputs.name: GET /agents/sdet-architect/runs/:id/migration
outputs.desc: `MIGRATION.md` as `text/markdown`, straight from the run's output JSON.

runbook.rerun: Deterministic: the same estate and options give the same bytes, so a second run after someone edits the legacy code is a clean diff of the generated project — that is how to see whether a refactor of the old suite raised or lowered coverage. Runs are never overwritten. With a local model configured, only the `suggestion:` comments next to TODOs can differ between runs; the code lines cannot.
runbook.integrate: Move `workspace/<run_id>/playwright` into the application repository, keep `MIGRATION.md` at its root as the work list, and wire the generated workflow into CI; it already sets `BASE_URL` from a repository variable with the detected default. Work the TODO list top-down, then delete the `NOTE(sdet-architect)` lines once the specs are green three runs in a row. To support another legacy dialect, add a parser that returns a `TestSuite` (see `parsers/selenium-python.ts` for a ~110-line example) and one `case` in `classifyFile` and `parseOne`; the planner, emitters and report need no change. In the engagement on the [process page](../process.html) this project is the regression layer that runs on every change during and after the pilot.
